messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: SEV-2 network degradation affecting private connectivity for customer AcmeCorp via PrivateConnect (us-east-2). Pager details: > 40% packet loss observed on VPN tunnel and intermittent BGP withdraws. Auto-runbook: collect pcap + BGP dumps.

sasha (oncall): acknowledging, jumping in. Can someone grab the initial BGP dumps and latest traceroutes? @maria please triage routing.

maria (netops): on it. grabbing BGP from the edge and the customer-facing router. seeing repeated AS path changes to AcmeCorp prefixes, looks like two upstreams flapping between us-east-2a and us-east-2b.

raj (infra): adding context: we had a maintenance window earlier today in us-east-2b for storage; shouldn't have touched networking but checking for correlated changes.

ingrid (customer-sre): Acme reports user sessions dropping and auth failures through PrivateLink — they see traffic route via secondary region intermittently. Customer impact: ~30% API errors for writes, reads mostly ok.

incident-bot: collected artifacts: /artifacts/1958754321/pcap-edge-1.gz, /artifacts/1958754321/bgpdump-edge.txt, /artifacts/1958754321/traceroutes.txt

maria (netops): quick dump excerpt: `BGP UPDATE: 203.0.113.0/24 withdrew from peer A, announced from peer B with MED change` repeating 3m intervals. probable route reflection/duplicate route advertisement between AZ routers.

sasha (oncall): Can we isolate by blackholing one of the paths temporarily or set LOCAL_PREF to prefer stable path? Need to avoid customer traffic blackhole if possible.

raj (infra): propose temporary route preference change: prefer us-east-2a (stable) by applying `set local-preference 200` on edge-router-azb for Acme prefixes. Will coordinate with cloud provider.

maria (netops): before making infra changes, check PrivateConnect/VPN policy — if we change LOCAL_PREF, customer might still failover. Also check if VRF leaking between AZs happening. Running `show ip bgp neighbors` now.

azure-net-bot: Notice: Azure fabric reports control-plane flaps in us-east-2b between 13:02 and 13:09 UTC. Event id: az-fab-78321. Root cause flagged as transient route-reflection storm in fabric.

ingrid (customer-sre): fyi, Acme prefers no visible reroutes — can we keep session continuity? If not, let them know planned mitigation.

kevin (sales-advocate): I’m on call with Acme's ops. They want ETA and workaround. Please provide a short status to pass along.

sasha (oncall): status for customer: partial impact to PrivateConnect flows (writes failing). We suspect cloud fabric route reflection causing asymmetric routing. Working on preferring one path and coordinating with cloud provider. ETA 30–45m for mitigation attempt.

maria (netops): executing temporary policy on our side: `route-map SET-PREF permit 10 
 match ip address ACL-ACME 
 set local-preference 200` applied to neighbor edge-peer-us-east-2a. Pushing now.

raj (infra): applied local-pref on edge-router-azb. Monitoring BGP state...

maria (netops): BGP converged. Ads for 203.0.113.0/24 now consistently prefer us-east-2a for 2 consecutive updates.

incident-bot: MONITOR: Observing traffic shift. Packet loss for Acme decreased from 42% -> 6% in 3 min.

ingrid (customer-sre): Acme confirms sessions returning, error rate dropping. They still see occasional auth timeouts ~1/10k requests.

sasha (oncall): great. keeping this thread for postmortem notes. Please keep collecting route dumps for 1h. Also request cloud provider to follow up on fabric event.

azure-net-bot: Follow-up ticket created with provider: INC-az-78321-FW. Provider acknowledges and will provide RCA in 72h.

maria (netops): note for postmortem: root cause likely transient route reflection in AZ fabric causing duplicate announcements and AS-path oscillation. Contributing factor: lack of strict BGP dampening on our private edge for Peer B. Action items: enable dampening for customer-facing peers, add community tagging to prevent cross-az re-advert.

raj (infra): also: runbook update: add step to prefer stable path via LOCAL_PREF while verifying customer session continuity; add explicit check to avoid asynchronous failover.

ingrid (customer-sre): I already notified Acme CS and gave customer-friendly summary. They requested a follow-up postmortem and impact window.

kevin (sales-advocate): thanks — passed to Acme execs. They appreciated quick mitigation.

sasha (oncall): handing off to maria for 1hr watch. I’ll be reachable if it re-escalates. @maria takeover?

maria (netops): taking watch. monitoring graphs and BGP. Will escalate if packet loss >10% or BGP flaps resume.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: sasha -> maria at 13:27 UTC.

sasha (oncall): closing pager. follow-up checklist: collect 1h traces, produce impact timeline, include cloud provider ticket id (INC-az-78321-FW), and publish postmortem draft to #postmortems when ready.

maria (netops): ack. uploading final artifacts and will open postmortem doc.

incident-bot: THREAD SUMMARY: mitigation succeeded by preferring us-east-2a via local-pref; provider flagged transient fabric route reflection; customer impact window ~13:02–13:25 UTC; partial service degradation for Acme (~30% write failures peak).
